name: HIP graph capture and replay for ROCm kernel launch overhead reduction
workarounds: HIP graph capture reduces kernel launch overhead by recording and replaying kernel sequences
Particularly effective for decode workloads with many small kernels
vLLM uses CUDA graph capture (HIP graph equivalent) on ROCm to reduce launch overhead
notes: HIP graph capture is the ROCm equivalent of CUDA graph capture. It records a sequence of kernel launches into a graph that can be replayed with a single launch, eliminating per-kernel launch overhead. This is particularly important for LLM inference decode, where each token generation involves many small kernel launches (RMSNorm, RoPE, GEMM, attention, sampling). The ROCm memory management documentation covers stream-ordered memory allocation and graph capture. vLLM's ROCm backend uses graph capture (compilation-config with cudagraph_mode) to reduce launch overhead. The vLLM blog shows '--compilation-config {"custom_ops": ["-rms_norm", "-quant_fp8"], "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' as a recommended configuration. HIP graphs are most beneficial when kernel launch overhead is a significant fraction of total execution time - typically at small batch sizes and short sequences.
